title: Free Time
description: Ten short stories about free time: a summer race, a rock group, movies, chess, photos, a trip by ship, an English club, science, a basketball game and a puzzle.

lessons.title: The Summer Race
lessons.summary: Emma trains on the school track for the town's summer race in June and runs her best time.
lessons.text:
Emma is 16 years old. She loves running. Every summer, her town has a big race in the park. This year, the race was on the last day of June.

In May and June, Emma ran 4 days a week. She ran on the track at her school. She ran around the track 12 times. That is as long as the race. Her average time was 26 minutes. She wanted a time under 25 minutes.

Her friend Nick ran with her on the track. He said, "You start too fast. You have a lot of energy at the start, but you need energy at the end too. Focus on your own race." So Emma tried to focus. She did not start too fast. Her average time got better every week.

On the day of the race, Emma and her mother walked to the park. They crossed a big street. Many people were already in the park. There were 300 people in the race. It was a beautiful summer morning, and the sun was already hot.

The race started at 8 in the morning. Many people ran very fast at the start. Emma did not. She kept her energy. She did not look at the other people. She focused on her own race.

Near the end, Emma saw the finish line. She ran toward it as fast as she could. Her mother was near the finish line. She called, "Go, Emma, go!" Emma ran toward her mother and crossed the line. Her time was 24 minutes! It was her best time ever. Emma was very happy.

Questions:
When was the race this year?
The race was on the last day of June.
Where did Emma run before the race?
She ran on the track at her school.
What was her average time?
Her average time was 26 minutes.
What did Nick tell Emma?
Nick told her to focus on her own race.
What did Emma and her mother cross on the way to the park?
They crossed a big street.
What was Emma's time in the race?
Her time was 24 minutes.

lessons.title: The First Performance
lessons.summary: Jake's rock group practices in a church room and plays its first performance on a stage at the town party.
lessons.text:
Jake is 17 years old. He plays music in a rock group with 3 friends. The leader of the group is his friend Lily. She writes the songs. Every week, the group has practice in a big room at the church near Jake's house. The people at the church are very nice. They let the group use the room for free.

One day, Lily came to practice with news. "We have our first performance!" she said. "We can play on the stage at the town party in 2 weeks." The friends were very happy. But Jake was also a little worried.

For 2 weeks, the group had practice every day after school. Lily was a good leader. She said, "Practice the hard parts again and again." Jake also practiced at home every night.

The night before the performance, Jake could not sleep. He thought about the stage and all the people. He thought about the hard parts of the songs. At 2 in the morning, he still could not sleep.

The day of the performance was very hot. In the afternoon, the group stood near the stage. It was hot there, and Jake was worried again. Lily looked at him and said, "Stay cool, Jake. We know these songs. We practiced them at the church for weeks."

Then the group walked onto the stage. They played 6 rock songs. The people in the park loved the music. After the last song, many people came to the stage. A young man said to Jake, "Your group is so cool!"

That night, Jake was very happy. He went to bed early, and he slept for 10 hours.

Questions:
Who is the leader of the group?
The leader of the group is Lily.
Where does the group have practice?
The group has practice in a big room at the church.
Where was the first performance?
It was on the stage at the town party.
Why could Jake not sleep?
He thought about the stage and all the people.
What did Lily say to Jake before the performance?
She said, "Stay cool, Jake."
How long did Jake sleep that night?
He slept for 10 hours.

lessons.title: An Article About a Movie
lessons.summary: Mia reads an article online about a new movie, sees it with her friend Sara, and writes her own article.
lessons.text:
Mia is 20 years old. She loves movies. Her favorite director is Ruth Martin. Mia knows every movie by this director. Every week, Mia also reads articles about movies online.

One day, Mia read an article online about a new movie by Ruth Martin. The title of the movie was "The Long Road." The article described the movie. It is a story about a father and his son. They travel across the country in an old car.

Mia called her friend Sara. "There is a new movie by Ruth Martin," Mia said. "Do you want to see it with me?"

"What is the title?" Sara asked.

"The title is 'The Long Road.'"

"Is it similar to her last movie?"

"Yes, it's likely to be similar. Her movies are always about families."

The next night, Mia and Sara went to see the movie. They both liked it a lot. The music was beautiful. After the movie, Sara did not understand one part. Mia explained it to her. Then Sara understood.

At home, Mia wrote her own article about the movie. She described the story and the music. She explained why she liked the movie. She also wrote that it is similar to the director's last movie, but better. Then she put her article online.

The next morning, there were 12 comments under her article. One comment was from Sara. It said, "Great article!" Another comment said, "I saw the movie too, and I liked it a lot." Mia read every comment. She was very happy. She will likely write more articles soon.

Questions:
Who is Mia's favorite director?
Her favorite director is Ruth Martin.
What was the title of the new movie?
The title was "The Long Road."
What did the article describe?
It described the movie.
What did Mia explain to Sara?
She explained one part of the movie.
Where did Mia put her own article?
She put it online.
How many comments were under her article?
There were 12 comments under her article.

lessons.title: The Chess Club Election
lessons.summary: Tom's chess society holds an election for a new leader, and Tom decides to vote for his friend Ben.
lessons.text:
Tom is 15 years old. He loves chess. Every week, he goes to the chess society in his town. The society has 30 members.

In chess, the king is the most important piece. If you lose your king, you lose the game. So Tom always watches his king.

Every year, the society has an election for a new leader. This year, 2 people wanted to be the leader: Ann Clark and Ben. Ann is 60 years old. Ben is 19, and he is Tom's friend.

Before the election, Tom and Ben played a game. "The white pieces are mine," Ben said.

"No, the white pieces are mine," Tom said. "You had them last week."

"Okay, you are right," Ben said.

Ben has a fast style. He likes to attack. Tom has a different style. He likes to think a lot before he moves. Later, Ben wanted to move his king. "I wouldn't move the king now," Tom said. But Ben moved it. That is a common problem for young players. A few moves later, Tom won the game. "You were right," Ben said. "Next time, I will listen to you."

Tom had to make a decision. Who was the best leader for the society? Ann was a good player. But Tom asked her, "Can you come every week?" Ann said, "No. I wouldn't have time for that." Ben came every week. He helped the young players, and he showed them their common problems. Tom trusted Ben.

On the day of the election, every member wrote a name on a piece of paper. Tom wrote "Ben." It was an easy decision for him.

Ben won the election. He said, "Thank you all. I will try to be a good leader for our society." Tom was very happy.

Questions:
How many members does the society have?
The society has 30 members.
What is the most important piece in chess?
The king is the most important piece.
What is Ben's style?
Ben has a fast style. He likes to attack.
What did Tom say when Ben wanted to move his king?
Tom said, "I wouldn't move the king now."
Why did Tom trust Ben?
Ben came every week, and he helped the young players.
Who won the election?
Ben won the election.

lessons.title: Photos in the East Part of Town
lessons.summary: Anna walks around the old east part of her city one morning and takes photos of buildings.
lessons.text:
Anna is 25 years old. In her free time, she takes photos. She loves to take photos of old buildings. Every week, she walks around her city and takes photos.

One morning, Anna went to the east part of the city. The east part is very old. There are many beautiful buildings there. The day was clear and beautiful. It was a good day for photos.

First, Anna saw an old brown building. Above the door, there was a small blue sign with the name of the street. Anna took a photo of the building. Then she took a photo of the blue sign above the door. She loves the small details of old buildings.

Next, she walked down a long street. There, she saw a big white building with a brown door. Above the door, there was a number: 1890. It was the year of the building. Anna looked at the details of the door. She took 3 photos of it.

At the end of the street, there was a beautiful old house with a lot of land around it. Anna wanted to walk closer to the house. But there was a sign near the street. It said, "Private Property." So Anna did not walk on the private property. She stood in the street and took a photo from there.

Later, Anna went home. She looked at all her photos. She had 80 photos of the east part of the city. Her best photo was the photo of the small blue sign above the brown door. She put this photo on her wall.

Questions:
What does Anna do in her free time?
She takes photos.
Where did Anna go one morning?
She went to the east part of the city.
What was above the door of the brown building?
There was a small blue sign above the door.
What did the sign near the street say?
It said, "Private Property."
How many photos did Anna have?
She had 80 photos.
What was her best photo?
It was the photo of the small blue sign above the brown door.

lessons.title: A Trip on a Ship
lessons.summary: Sam and his friend Max travel across the water on a ship, open their room with a key card and play cards.
lessons.text:
Sam and his friend Max are 22 years old. They love to travel. This summer, they wanted to travel to a small town across the water. The best way to travel there was by ship.

Early one morning, they went to the ship. Before they could enter the ship, they went through security. A security man looked in their bags. Then a woman at the door of the ship asked for their tickets. Sam and Max showed their tickets, and they entered the ship.

Inside, a man gave Sam a key card. "This is the key to your room," he said. "It is room 210." Sam and Max walked to room 210. Sam put the key card on the door, and the door opened. The room was small, but it was nice. It had 2 beds and a big window.

The trip across the water took 8 hours. After 1 hour, Sam wanted to call his mother. But his phone was dead. "My phone is dead too," Max said. So the friends found a box of cards in the room. They played cards for 3 hours. Max won most of the games.

In the afternoon, the friends went outside. They stood near the side of the ship and looked across the water. It was beautiful.

Many hours later, the ship came to the town. Sam and Max went back to their room. Sam put the key card on the door again. They took their bags. Then they gave the key card back to the man. The friends walked off the ship. They were very happy. They love to travel together.

Questions:
How did Sam and Max travel to the town?
They traveled by ship.
What did they go through before they entered the ship?
They went through security.
What did the man give Sam?
He gave Sam a key card.
Why could Sam not call his mother?
His phone was dead.
What did the friends play?
They played cards.
How long did the trip across the water take?
It took 8 hours.

lessons.title: The English Club
lessons.summary: Yuki, a student from Japan, goes to a free English club and does a role play with a new friend.
lessons.text:
Yuki is 21 years old. She is from Japan, and now she is a student at a college in Boston. English is not her first language. She can read English well, but speaking is hard for her.

One day, Yuki saw a sign at her college. It said, "Free English Club. Practice the language with new friends!" So the next week, she went to the club.

There were 15 people in the club. They came from many countries. Their teacher was a woman named Kate. "Hello, everyone," Kate said. "Every week, we do a new activity. Today the activity is a role play. Let's start!"

"Let's make groups of 2," Kate said. Yuki was with a man from Brazil named Paulo. In the role play, Paulo's role was a man at a store. Yuki's role was a person who wanted to buy a bag. "Good morning," Yuki said. "What's the price of this bag?" Paulo answered, "It's 30 dollars."

Sometimes Yuki's English did not make sense. Then Kate helped her. Kate gave individual help to each person. "Don't worry," Kate said to Yuki. "You'll learn fast. You'll see."

After the role play, Kate said, "Now let's do a second activity." Each person asked the other person in the group personal questions. "What's your name? What's your favorite food? What do you do in your free time?" Yuki asked Paulo personal questions, and he asked her. It all made sense to her.

At the end, Kate said, "Thank you, everyone. You'll all speak this language very well soon." Yuki was very happy. She made a new friend, and she used her English. Now she goes to the club every week.

Questions:
Where is Yuki from?
Yuki is from Japan.
What was the first activity at the club?
The first activity was a role play.
What was Yuki's role in the role play?
Her role was a person who wanted to buy a bag.
What did Kate give each person?
She gave individual help to each person.
What was the second activity?
Each person asked the other person in the group personal questions.
What did Kate say to Yuki?
She said, "You'll learn fast."

lessons.title: The Paper Bridge
lessons.summary: At his science club, Leo builds a bridge out of paper that holds the most books.
lessons.text:
Leo is 11 years old. He loves science. Every week, he goes to a science club at his school. The leader of the club is Dan Ross. This month, Dan had a new project for the children.

"Each child must produce a bridge," Dan said. "But there is one condition. You can only use 1 material: paper. Every child gets the same amount of paper: 10 pieces of standard paper. Standard paper is the paper we use every day at school."

Leo wanted to produce the best bridge in the club. After school, he went to a store with his father. The store had a big range of paper. There was paper in a range of sizes, from very small to very large. Leo looked at all of it. But he remembered the condition. He could only use standard paper, so he did not buy any paper. Instead, he bought a book about bridges.

At home, Leo read the book. He learned that the form of a material is very important. One piece of paper is not strong. But paper in a round form is very strong. So Leo made round parts from his paper. He made many small round parts of the same size. Each part used only a small amount of paper. Then he put them together.

On the day of the test, every child had a bridge. The bridges were all different sizes. Dan put books on each bridge, one by one. Most bridges fell after 3 or 4 books. Leo's bridge held 12 books! No other bridge held so many books.

Dan said, "Leo, you had the same amount of paper as everyone, but you produced a very strong bridge. You understand science." Leo was very happy.

Questions:
What does Leo love?
Leo loves science.
What was the condition for the project?
The children could only use 1 material: paper.
What did the store have?
The store had a big range of paper.
Why did Leo not buy any paper?
He could only use standard paper.
What did Leo make from his paper?
He made many small round parts of the same size.
How many books did Leo's bridge hold?
His bridge held 12 books.

lessons.title: The Big Game
lessons.summary: Kevin's basketball team plays in the first round of the city games, and Kevin passes the ball instead of throwing it himself.
lessons.text:
Kevin is 14 years old. He plays basketball for his school team. He loves the game, especially the big games. But Kevin hates losing. When his team loses, he is not happy for days.

This year, Kevin's team was in the city games. 16 teams were in the first round. In the first round, Kevin's team played against a team from the north part of the city. That team was very good, especially their big players.

The game started. Kevin had the ball a lot. He wanted to score. He tried to throw the ball into the basket again and again. But many of his throws were bad. One throw was so bad that the ball fell to the ground. After the first half, the score was 30 to 22 for the other team.

Kevin's friend Chris said, "Kevin, you don't have to score every time. Instead, pass the ball to me. I am open." Kevin did not like this idea at first. He wanted to score. But he hated losing more.

In the second half, Kevin played a different game. He did not throw the ball every time. Instead, he passed the ball to Chris and the other players. Chris scored again and again. Once Kevin fell to the ground, but he got up fast and kept playing.

At the end of the game, the score was 50 to 46. Kevin's team won! They beat a very good team. Kevin scored a total of 10 points, and Chris scored a total of 20 points.

After the game, Kevin said to Chris, "Thank you. We beat them together." Next week, the team will play in the second round.

Questions:
What does Kevin hate?
Kevin hates losing.
How many teams were in the first round?
16 teams were in the first round.
What was the score after the first half?
The score was 30 to 22 for the other team.
What did Kevin do instead of throwing the ball every time?
He passed the ball to Chris and the other players.
How many points did Kevin score in total?
He scored a total of 10 points.
Which team won the game?
Kevin's team won. They beat a very good team.

lessons.title: The Puzzle
lessons.summary: After an operation, Joe has to stay inside, so his grandchild Lucy brings him a puzzle with 500 pieces.
lessons.text:
Joe is 75 years old. He loves to be outside. Every day, he walks in the park, and he works outside near his house.

In June, Joe had an operation on his foot. The operation went well. After the operation, the doctor said, "Joe, you must stay inside for 2 weeks. You can't walk a lot. Rest your foot." Joe was not happy. He did not want to stay inside. He wanted to be outside.

For 3 days, Joe stayed inside and watched television. He did not like it. Then his grandchild Lucy came to see him. She had a big box. "Can you guess what's in the box?" she asked.

Joe tried to guess. "A book?" he asked.

"No," Lucy said. "Guess again."

"A movie?"

"No! It's a puzzle. It has 500 pieces. You put the pieces together, and they make a picture."

They opened the box. The picture was of a beautiful park in summer. There were 500 small pieces. Lucy and Joe found a big table. Every day after school, Lucy came. She and Joe worked on the puzzle together. They looked at each piece. Then they pressed the piece into the right place.

After 10 days, there was only 1 piece left. Lucy gave it to Joe. Joe pressed the last piece into its place. The picture was perfect. "It's perfect," Lucy said. "It's a perfect park," Joe said. "And soon I can go to the real park again."

2 weeks after the operation, Joe went back to the doctor. The doctor said, "Your foot is perfect now. You can go outside." Joe was very happy. The next day, he walked to the park with Lucy.

Questions:
Where does Joe love to be?
He loves to be outside.
What did the doctor say after the operation?
The doctor said, "You must stay inside for 2 weeks."
What did Lucy ask Joe to guess?
She asked him to guess what was in the box.
How many pieces did the puzzle have?
The puzzle had 500 pieces.
What did Joe do with the last piece?
He pressed the last piece into its place.
What did the doctor say 2 weeks after the operation?
The doctor said, "Your foot is perfect now."
